---
title: "Stage 3 – The claim and its reproduction"
case: housing
---
In this stage you write the estimand statement behind the claim, finish the causal graph of the experiment, and reproduce the value recorded in the SCORE robustness study (Aczel et al. 2026) for one of the five analysts, whichever you choose.

## 1. The exercise

[Read the exercise page](exercise.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

## 2. Task 2 – The data, the estimand and the graph

**In your report**, in the two boxes of Task 2 of `index.qmd`, or in your working script. Count what came back for each name, complete the estimand statement, and put the questions of the second box to the causal graph of `R/dag_starter.R`.

[Open the webR workspace at Task 2](../../lab.qmd#task-2-data){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

## 3. Task 3 – The reproduction

**In your report**, in Task 3 of `index.qmd`. Choose one of the five analysts and reproduce the analysis in the tab of that analyst. Working alone, you can take a second analyst whose test differs from the first.

[Open the webR workspace at Task 3](../../lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

## 4. The continuity correction

**In the webR workspace**, at [Defaults and codings](../../lab.qmd#task-3-defaults){target="_blank"}, whose cells run both tests without the correction.

## 5. Audit experiments

[Open Audit experiments](../../companion/experiments.qmd#sec-audits){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work from [Audit and correspondence studies](../../companion/experiments.qmd#sec-audits) to [Comparing among replies](../../companion/experiments.qmd#sec-posttreatment). The tasks do not need section 3, which simulates the experiment with DeclareDesign, or the second simulation in section 5, and you can leave both until the route is done.

[Open Binary outcomes](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd#sec-outcome){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work from [A yes-or-no outcome](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd#sec-outcome) to [The methods side by side](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd#sec-side-by-side).

## 7. Causal graphs

[Open Causal graphs and adjustment sets](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-arrows){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Work from [Arrows as claims](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-arrows) to [Counting all delivered emails](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-all-emails).

## 8. The decision map

[Open the decision map](../../menu.qmd#map){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The map prepares Task 4 in the next stage.

**Shortcuts.** If you know logistic regression and odds ratios, take from the binary-outcomes module only the sections on [odds ratios and covariates](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd#sec-collapsibility) and [the methods side by side](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd#sec-side-by-side). If you have drawn causal graphs before, take from the graph module only [Conditioning on a reply](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-collider) and [The graph of the case study](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-case).
